chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Harith, Abu Bakr al-Wasiti, from the origin of his book, told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Sulaym told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban told us, saying: Abu Mariam told us, from 'Ata', from Ibn Abbas, saying:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Allah is my Lord, and there is no sign for me with Him, and I am the Messenger of my Lord, and there is no sign with me, and Ali is my Ally and the Ally of whoever I am his Ally, and there is no sign with him.

key_terms.وَلِيُّ مَنْ كُنْتُ وَلِيَّهُ: The Ally of whoever I am his Ally

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Ali being the Wali of the Prophet according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ma'ani al-Akhbar establishes the principle of 'Amara' (divine authentication) by contrasting the Prophet's mission with Ali's vicegerency; while the Prophet carried no physical sign, Ali's authority is validated by the absence of such a need, implying an intrinsic, divine legitimacy. It underscores the Shia doctrine that Ali's Wilayah is not merely political but a spiritual station confirmed by God, distinct from the prophetic seal of authenticity. This narration reinforces the concept that the Imam's authority is self-evident and divinely ordained, requiring no external proof beyond his appointment.
